reason: I want to restore the radio, and the service tool seems suited to straightening or repairing the bent antenna.
expectation: I expect the tool to make the antenna usable, though it may still need mounting or further work.

alternatives.reason: Charging the emergency battery could help prepare for night, but the antenna is an obvious obstacle to hearing Earth's message.
The foil and felt may make window insulation, but I want to start with the radio.

effect: The antenna is straightened, so mounting it is the next plausible step toward restoring the radio.
reaction: That result was predictable and reassuring.
reason: The radio mount is the natural place to install the straightened antenna and advance the radio goal.
expectation: I expect the antenna to be mounted, though the radio may need further work before it receives a message.

alternatives.reason: Charging the battery could help with nighttime readiness, but I want to continue the radio repair.
The foil and felt could insulate the window, but the antenna is ready to mount now.

effect: Mounting the antenna restored the radio, completing that goal. I can now focus on preparing the cabin for night.
reaction: The twelve-minute-old message makes the distance from Earth feel tangible, and I’m curious what the reply will say.
reason: The foil and felt seem useful for insulating the window, which is losing heat.
expectation: I expect them to form an insulating covering, though it may need a way to mount it.

alternatives.reason: Charging the battery also seems useful for night, but the window is a known source of heat loss.

effect: The foil and felt became reflective quilt stock, which appears ready to be made into a window covering.
reaction: The result fits my expectation, though I’m curious how the rail will be used.
reason: Combining the quilt stock with the curtain rail seems like a practical way to make a covering for the heat-losing window.
expectation: I expect a mountable insulating curtain, though it may still need to be installed at the window.

alternatives.reason: Charging the battery may also help prepare for night, but I want to finish the window covering first.

effect: The rail and quilt stock made a hanging window quilt, ready to install at the window.
reaction: The result matched my expectation and feels like a natural next step.
reason: Installing the quilt should help reduce heat loss through the cabin window.
expectation: I expect the quilt to cover the window and contribute to nighttime readiness, though charging the battery may still be needed.

alternatives.reason: Charging the battery also seems useful for night, but the window covering is ready to install.

effect: The quilt is installed and slides across the window, reducing the felt cold. Nighttime readiness is still incomplete, so charging the battery is the remaining offered action.
reaction: The cold easing and the curtain sliding back in the morning make the improvement feel tangible.
reason: Charging the emergency battery seems useful for keeping the cabin ready for night, and it is the only offered combination.
expectation: I expect the array to charge the battery and possibly complete the nighttime readiness goal.

effect: Charging the battery completed nighttime readiness and clarified that a supplied fuel-cell backup can sustain essential systems through a dark spell.
reaction: The connection to the recovered array is satisfying, though the fuel-cell backup was new information.

mostWorthwhile.text: Restoring the radio was most worthwhile: the twelve-minute-old message made Mars's distance from Earth tangible and left me curious about the reply.

leastWorthwhile.text: Making and installing the window quilt felt a little repetitive, although the description of the cold easing gave the finished result a tangible payoff.

surprise.text: The message being twelve minutes old made the communication delay feel real; I was also surprised to learn about the supplied fuel-cell backup.

arbitrary.text: None of the actions felt particularly arbitrary. The repair and insulation steps had clear purposes, though charging the battery became the only offered combination at the end.

continue.text: Yes. I would continue to learn what Earth's reply says and see how the expedition develops.
